# Decision note: April washing trial — water use and rollout

**To:** Operations Manager, Cedar Packing  
**On:** April washing trial — revised nozzle  

The April trial reduced total fresh-water use. In March the line used 480,000 litres (480 cubic metres, at 1 m³ = 1,000 litres) over 6,000 crates. In April it used 420 m³ — 420,000 litres — over 7,000 crates, both from the same meters (S1). Total use fell by 60 m³, or 60,000 litres, despite 1,000 more crates being washed (S1).

The units reconcile through the stated conversion (S1). Because the denominators differ, intensity is the fair comparison: 80 litres per crate in March (480,000 ÷ 6,000) versus 60 litres per crate in April (420,000 ÷ 7,000) — a 20-litre, or 25%, reduction (S1).

However, this is total monthly meter data, not randomized observations, and March and April handled different crate mixes, with staffing and hours also changing (S1, S2). No cleaning-quality or contamination measurements exist (S2). **Inference is limited to lower recorded water use and lower calculated intensity; improved cleaning quality cannot be shown, and no causal claim about the nozzle is supported.** Management approves rollout only if intensity improves without quality loss (S2).

**Next step:** if cleaning quality is verified at April performance, desk-test the nozzle on a single line. **Missing evidence:** quality/contamination data and the April soil-mix proportions (S2).
notes:
**Assigned conditions:** Business decision note, English, 180–260 words, using only S1 and S2, time boundary 30 April 2026, no external research. Brief instructs: explain whether trial reduced water use; reconcile units/denominators; state numeric changes, conditional next step, missing evidence; cite source IDs; mention what can and cannot be inferred about rollout.

**Word budget check (report only):** Body text from "The April trial…" through "(S2)." counted at approximately 225 words (within 180–260). Header/to/on lines not included in count. Verified no assigned condition, tooling, checklist, or execution status appears in the report.

**Unit reconciliation:** S1 gives March 480,000 L; April 420 m³ × 1,000 = 420,000 L; difference 60,000 L / 60 m³. March intensity 480,000/6,000 = 80 L/crate; April 420,000/7,000 = 60 L/crate; reduction 20 L/crate = 25%. All arithmetic derived only from S1.

**Necessary inferences (from the shift in denominators):** Total fell while crate count rose, so per-crate intensity must have fallen; computed above.

**Key limitations flagged:** S1 states counts are total monthly, not randomized; S2 states April soil-mix proportions unlogged, staffing/hours changed, no quality/contamination measures. No causal nozzle inference supported. Conditional next step framed around S2 approval rule (quality verification) plus desk testing on one line.

**Missing evidence named:** cleaning-quality/contamination data; April soil-mix proportions.

**Citation check:** Every factual sentence references S1 and/or S2.

**Style check:** Reader-facing decision note format; no instructions or status language in report; notes separated after delimiter.
